newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Rains seen favouring Ivorian cocoa crop.
newsitem.headline: Rains seen favouring Ivorian cocoa crop.

text.p: Light rains in southern Ivorian cocoa areas this week favoured 1997/98 (Oct-Sept) crop prospects after a dry start to August, crop analysts said.
Rains fell in the commercial capital, Abidjan, on Monday and Tuesday after showers there and in many other areas at the weekend.
Buyers in other southern areas on Tuesday also reported showers and cloud cover, both of which are needed to keep up soil moisture for pod growth.

"There is still moisture in the soil if you kick away the leaves and no sign of dust," a crop analyst told Reuters after returning from an up-country tour at the weekend. Breezes in some areas had threatened to raise evaporation rates.

The rains this week coincided with the arrival of U.S.-based private crop analyst Hans Kilian's team for a tour of Ivorian plantations and a chance to update 1997/98 main crop (Oct-April) forecasts, industry sources said.

Other crop analysts said occasional light rains into September should confirm a large main crop from October, despite the possibility of dry weather later this year from El Nino weather patterns already affecting other parts of the world.

One said the 1997/98 main crop might exceed one million tonnes, at least equal to about 1.01 million in 1996/97 and similar to levels in the record 1995/96 year, when the total crop ended at 1.2 million tonnes.
Kilian in June put the 1997/98 main crop at 0.785 million tonnes, but forecasts were usually adjusted as seasons drew closer, traders said at the time.
Any early signs of drier El Nino weather would be closely watched over the next few weeks.
National forecasters said no rain fell in Abidjan during the first 10 days of August. Showers had been concentrated in more northerly cocoa areas.
Ivory Coast's short July-August dry season was preceded by heavy late-June rains. Subsequent cool air temperatures helped soil water retention.
National data show rains over the 30 days to August 10 fluctuated around an average of 20 mm in each of three 10-day periods.
